newsitem.title: USA: XATA sees more modest growth for FY97.
newsitem.headline: XATA sees more modest growth for FY97.

text.p: XATA Corp, a producer of onboard information systems for the fleet trucking industry, said Tuesday the increase in its fiscal 1997 net income and revenue from fiscal 1996 levels will be more modest than previously expected.
For the December 31 first quarter, the company's sales rose 8.3 percent to $2.5 million. Net income declined to $26,753 or $0.01 a share from $270,726 or $0.07 a share in the same year-ago period.

President Dennis Johnson said sales to private fleet customers were more than double the fiscal 1996 first-quarter level. This growth partly offset a slowdown in deliveries to a large customer that is currently involved in a major restructuring. Deliveries to this customer accounted for more than 45 percent of fiscal 1996 revenue but only 15 percent of first-quarter revenue.
Johnson said in a statement deliveries to this customer will remain significantly below the prior year's levels through the first quarter of fiscal 1998.

"While this slowdown is disappointing, the customer remains committed to our system as a key component of its logistics management solution and continues to report an attractive return on its investment in our products," he added. A slowdown in deliveries under the major contract and expenses related to the acquisitions of Key Logistics and Payne & Associates resulted in the decline in first-quarter net income, Johnson said.

"As we expected, these acquired businesses are not yet contributing to net income. However, they bring us technology and capabilities that strategically fit our focus on becoming a full-service logistics solution provider," he added.
